title: Enterprise trust briefing: seller talking points and evidence checklist for inference platforms
body:
Purpose and audience:
This doc is a concise, field-ready briefing for sellers, solutions engineers, and CSEs when discussing security and compliance for Redwood Inference with enterprise buyers (legal, security, and platform teams). It translates technical controls into buyer-friendly evidence, outlines likely objections, and provides a compact audit-log language and evidence checklist for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA reviews.

High-level narrative (30-second elevator):
- We design inference for production-grade trust: predictable performance plus machine-verifiable controls for data handling and auditing.
- Customers choose Redwood when they need both operational SLAs and clear, engineer-level evidence for audits: scoped retention, immutable audit-trails, encryption-in-transit/at-rest, and optional private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data.

Key buyer concerns we anticipate (and short rebuttals):
- Data residency / where is my data stored?
  Response: Region pinning per deployment, data plane isolated per customer in Dedicated and Private modes; hosted API provides regional options with documented egress and storage locations.
- Can you prove you don't look at my requests?
  Response: We publish our data handling policy, provide customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments, and offer token-level telemetry without payload inspection; audit artifacts show access logs and operator actions.
- How are you handling PHI / HIPAA data?
  Response: We have a HIPAA readiness kit: BAAs available for Dedicated/Private, encrypted key management options, logging of access to PHI-involving routes, and redaction hooks to minimize PHI in logs.

Competitive differentiators to emphasize (positioning vs cloud vendors and LLM APIs):
- Unified trust model across deployment modes: same API, same observability contracts whether hosted, dedicated, or private.
- Engineer-verifiable artifacts: we provide pre-built evidence bundles (config exports, packing lists, audit-log extracts) tailored to SOC2/ISO auditors, not just policy pages.
- Inference-first SLOs + graceful degradation: when capacity or variants change we surface automatic fallbacks and show audit trails for routing decisions (who/why/when).

Practical guidance: tailoring the message by buyer persona
- CTO / Platform: emphasize private deployment, KMS/HSM support, network isolation, deployment automation (Terraform modules), and model pinning/rollouts.
- CISO / Security: emphasize SOC2 controls mapping, retention and deletion guarantees, immutable audit trails, RBAC + OPA/Gatekeeper hooks, and third-party penetration testing cadence.
- Legal / Procurement: emphasize contractual artifacts: BAA (for HIPAA), data processing addendum (DPA), and SOC2/ISO summary plus sample audit extracts.

Audit-log language (recommended schema to offer auditors) — copy-paste friendly
- Provide auditors a single example CSV/JSON export with the following columns/keys:
  - timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
  - request_id: stable uuid per request
  - customer_id: opaque customer identifier
  - tenant_request_hash: sha256 of the plaintext request (if allowed) or redacted placeholder
  - model_id: model tag/version used (e.g., gpt-like-13b-q4)
  - model_build_hash: artifact hash for model binary used for inference
  - route: API route invoked (text-generation, embeddings, chat)
  - tokens_in: integer
  - tokens_out: integer
  - response_size_bytes: integer
  - serving_node_id: instance id or pool id
  - region: cloud region or datacenter id
  - retention_policy_days: effective retention setting for that request
  - actor: user/service identity that triggered request (pseudonymized if required)
  - access_type: api-key | oauth | internal-service
  - operator_actions: human operator actions touching infrastructure (create, update, delete)
  - integrity_proof: sha256 signature over the exported row + export metadata (optional)

Notes on privacy and redaction:
- For regulated datasets we recommend returning tenant_request_hash rather than plaintext. The hash proves request evidence without exposing content.
- Provide a documented, repeatable redaction algorithm when customers request removal of PII/PHI from logs. Include a deterministic mapping table for request_id -> redacted_id for audit continuity.

Evidence checklist (what to include in a seller-provided bundle):
- Configuration exports: deployment config, model pinning config, retention policy settings (JSON/Terraform snippets).
- Sample audit-log export (as described above) covering a configurable time window.
- Access-control proof: RBAC role list and a screenshot or export of policy bindings for the requested tenant.
- KMS integration proof: key creation and rotation logs, sample KMS policy or HSM appliance detail (if private).
- Network diagram: VPC/subnet mapping, peering/VPN screenshots, and ingress/egress controls.
- Incident response summary: playbook excerpt, notification SLAs, and most recent tabletop exercise date.
- Pen test / vuln scan summary: high-level findings, remediation dates.

SOC2 / ISO / HIPAA readiness mapping (seller cheat-sheet)
- SOC2 Type II: we map our observability and change-control artifacts to CC6 and CC7 style controls — provide auditor-friendly exports: access logs (CC6), change management tickets and git commits for infra changes (CC7), and monitoring alerts and SLAs for availability (CC3).
- ISO27001: provide Statement of Applicability extracts, control owners list, and the top-level risk register summary.
- HIPAA: BAA options for Dedicated/Private, sample PHI handling playbook, redaction snippets and evidence for encryption at rest/in transit.

Seller scripts and quick answers (copyable)
- "Do you keep customer prompts?" -> "We do not use customer data to train models. For hosted customers we keep telemetry and audit logs per configured retention windows; we can provide hashed or redacted exports on request. Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger isolation and can integrate with customer KMS for key control."
- "What if an auditor asks for raw logs?" -> "We deliver an agreed export with schema fields that balance audit requirements and privacy — we can include hashed request artifacts and integrity proofs. For PHI we will follow the redaction and BAA process before any transfer."

Common objections and rebuttals (detailed)
- Objection: "We require 7 years of unredacted logs."
  Rebuttal: "Long-term retention of unredacted logs is a controllable policy. Redwood supports flexible retention settings; however, for PHI and regulated PII we typically recommend hashed or encrypted retention and a documented request process for access. We can propose a contractual SLR for extended archival on Dedicated deployments."
- Objection: "How can you prove model provenance for an audit?"
  Rebuttal: "We provide model build hashes, container image digests, and deployment rollouts. Our release artifacts include model version, training provenance metadata where available, and runtime kernel selection records. All of this can be included in an evidence bundle for an auditor."

Playbook for a CSE / SE during an audit kickoff call (10 minute checklist)
1) Ask which controls the auditor will focus on (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA) and preferred artifact formats.
2) Confirm scope: which tenants, routes, time windows, and whether PHI is in scope.
3) Offer a default evidence bundle and timeline: sample logs + config exports within 3 business days, deeper artifacts (KMS, infra commits) within 7 business days.
4) Establish redaction rules and point of contact for custodian signatures.
5) Lock in retention semantics and any contractual amendments (BAA/DPA).

Appendix: suggested retention + redaction policy language for contracts (short form)
- "Redwood will retain audit logs for an initial period of X days (default 90), configurable by the customer up to a contractual maximum. For data classified as PHI, logs will be stored in encrypted form and accessed only under documented administrative controls. On deletion requests, Redwood will either delete or cryptographically erase searchable payloads in accordance with agreed processes and will provide a deletion certificate within Y days."

Next steps for GTM:
- Turn this doc into a one-page "evidence kit" checklist and a ready-to-send zip template with sample logs, a config export, and a copy of the DPA/BAA.
- Coordinate with Applied ML and SRE to finalize a canonical audit-log export sample.
- Build a short enablement deck (5–7 slides) and rehearse with AE/CSE pairs.

Open questions for product/security to resolve (for next revision):
- Standardize integrity_proof mechanism and sample signing key management for exported evidence.
- Finalize the default retention windows exposed in the Console vs. API and contract language.
- Agree on an official pen-test summary redaction level we can share in sales cycles.

Owner notes: this is intentionally practical and copyable. Keep the next iteration lean: produce the zip template and a one-page cheat-sheet for AEs.
